# Codex Integration Requirements Checklist: Codex CLI Trace Support

**Purpose**: Validate the quality and completeness of the requirements/design for ingesting Codex
CLI's OTLP telemetry, computing its cost, and configuring it via `--setup`, before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-09-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md), [data-model.md](../data-model.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for every Codex OTLP event category needed to reconstruct a
      full turn (start, prompt, tool, completion), not just a subset? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for what happens when Codex reports a turn with zero tool
      calls (a pure Q&A turn)? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for how the `--setup` step reports its outcome to the user
      in each of the five documented `config.toml` states? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, FR-009]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for what "consistent with the computation approach used for
      other tools" means when a Codex model has no direct Anthropic/Copilot analog? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "the working-directory information present in Codex's OTLP payload" specific
      enough to be unambiguous about which attribute key(s) qualify? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "a documented default rate" for unknown models quantified (a specific number) or
      left as an implementation-time decision? [Ambiguity, Spec §US3 AC2]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "the appropriate tool-call type" in FR-004 clear about which categories apply to
      Codex's own tool/command vocabulary, versus assuming Copilot/Claude's categories transfer
      unchanged? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Are the project-auto-detection requirements in FR-003 consistent with the fallback
      behavior described in the Edge Cases section (no silent contradiction between "must detect"
      and "falls back when missing")? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the segregation requirements in FR-011 and the Codex Session key-entity
      description consistent about what uniquely identifies a session when two tools run in the
      same directory? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Key Entities]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK010 Can SC-001 ("no manual file editing") be objectively verified without relying on the
      implementer's own account of what counts as "manual"? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK011 Can SC-003's "rounding tolerance" be checked without a stated numeric tolerance value?
      [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK012 Is SC-005 ("never crashes... or blocks ingestion") paired with a concrete observable
      signal (e.g., process still responding, subsequent event still recorded) rather than a
      subjective judgment? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for a Codex turn that errors out (non-zero exit / failed
      tool) rather than completing normally? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements defined for the out-of-order-event scenario named in Edge Cases
      beyond restating the question (i.e., what the system should actually do)? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for a Codex CLI version upgrade that changes attribute names
      the parser already depends on, beyond "ignore unrecognized events"? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK016 Are there any explicit requirements bounding how much Codex OTLP payload size/rate the
      ingestion path must tolerate, or is this intentionally left unspecified? [Gap, NFR]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for whether Codex prompt/response content capture is
      expected to be configurable (privacy), matching the existing content-capture toggle pattern
      used for other tools? [Gap, Security/Privacy]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK018 Is the assumption that Codex's OTLP event names/attributes match the cited public
      source flagged as something to reconfirm against the installed Codex CLI version, rather
      than treated as guaranteed stable? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the dependency on Codex CLI requiring config-file (not env-var) telemetry setup
      validated against the specific Codex CLI version the user is expected to run, given this is
      a fast-moving external tool? [Dependency, Assumption]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK020 Is there a defined requirement & acceptance-criteria ID scheme consistently applied
      across spec/plan/data-model so a future reviewer can trace an implementation decision back to
      a specific FR/SC? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
